about: The first duplicate scan of the SAT pack (scripts/scan_duplicates.py), Nov 9, 2026: what was compared, what it found, what was done.
compared: Every pair of items within a section. Math by stem, table, figure elements and choices; Reading and Writing by passage, paired passage and choices (stems repeat by design). Word 3-shingles, Jaccard weighted by rarity, numbers kept (same) and folded (shape). Thresholds: duplicate = same answer with same ≥ 0.40 or shape ≥ 0.80; near-copy = same ≥ 0.50; template = shape ≥ 0.80 (listed only); topic = passages with same ≥ 0.15 (listed only).

duplicates: the same question word for word, across two skills
the same polynomial graph and answer
the same cylinder (3 by 8) and answer
the third 'how many solutions' graph answering Zero
near_copies: clock-hand angles at 4:00 and 2:30; kept, see duplicates-allowed.json
the same garden story in two skills (found in the listing under the threshold)
found.templates: 43 Math pairs share a template with different numbers and answers (systems of equations, 'what value of x satisfies', graph readings); kept, they are the skill's standard forms.
found.topics: 13 passage pairs share a subject and opening across skills: the Three Sisters planting (6 items), the Montgomery bus boycott (5), the Silk Road (3), Antarctic ice cores, arctic terns, bunraku, 1800s factory hours, bread yeast (2 each).

rewritten.about: Twenty items replaced on Nov 9, 2026. Each went through: a writer (new content, same id, skill, difficulty, type and answer letter), check_items.py, a blind solve by a separate reviewer that had to reach the key, and an adversarial review; items the review sent back were revised and solved again. Three small final touches were made by hand after the reviews (a figure label moved clear of a tick label, a hint reworded so it no longer assumed the lines meet, and two pronouns replaced with 'the batch'), each re-checked with check_items.py.

rewritten.after: The scan reports no duplicate, near-copy or shared-subject pair beyond the one allowed pair; 42 Math pairs still share a template with different numbers and answers, which is how drill items are.

pipeline: Each replacement: written to the item format with new content; check_items.py (schema, choices, figure, passage rules, check code); a blind solve by a separate reviewer that had to reach the key; an adversarial review for a second defensible answer, figure/stem/key agreement, factual errors, difficulty and closeness to siblings; the answer kept the old item's letter so the file's balance holds.
